findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT- There were mouse droppings observed to be in the dry storage area behind the shelving. The PIC stated that maintenance is in charge of cleaning. There were multiple mouse traps observed throughout this dry storage area and in other areas in the kitchen. A follow up is scheduled for 9/24/2026 to ensure that the mouse droppings have been cleaned up. Ensure that mouse droppings are being regularly cleaned up to allow for proper monitoring of rodent presence.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed mice droppings on the floor in the storage area behind the shelves. Person-in-charge (PIC) stated the facility was deep cleaned recently, however there were still traces of mice droppings. The inspectors instructed the PIC to contact their pest control operatives for mice inspection and also clean the mice droppings. Inspectors will be back in 2 weeks to spot check for mice droppings. Ensure the facility is free of pests and their droppings.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed light to be passing through the lower part of the back door. The PIC was informed to seal the opening. Ensure light from outside do not pass through doors or other entrances in the facility to prevent potential entry of insects and rodents.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: The taco meat in the warmer was observed to only be holding at 131F (probed). The PIC stated that the warmer was turned down lower than it should be at due to them not wanting the plastic of the cups to melt. CORRECTED- The PIC reheated the taco meat to 165F and turned the warmer up to hold at 135F and above. Ensure that hot food is holding at 135F and above.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Inspector observed a pair of tongs previously handled by a student with bare hands fall into the pan of breadsticks. The employee stated that the next student could reach into the pan of breadsticks in order to take the tongs and serve herself a breadstick. Inspector stepped in and directed the employee with gloves to take the tongs and serve the student the breadstick on top left side which had not been contaminated by the soiled tongs. That was the last student in the line. Employee removed her gloves and stated that she would take the tongs to dish and wash her hands to re-glove without prompting.  Bread sticks left in the pan were discarded in the garbage and the pan taken to dish. Manager was consulted and she directed the crew running the window to place the breadstick on top of the chicken for service. Take great care to protect food when allowing students to serve themselves. The violation is considered corrected on site. 

3-304.11: (A) FOOD shall only contact surfaces of EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS that are cleaned. (B) SINGLE-SERVICE/USE ARTICLES (C) LINENS

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Inspector observed that the internal temperature of chicken nuggets is 119F. The warmers were turned down this morning due to the handling of bagels for breakfast. Chicken was cooked to 191F according to the logs kept by the facility. The chicken was added to the unit at 9am and service will be completed by 12:30pm. (3.5 hours) The facility will discard any food left at the end of the day. Inspector directed staff to turn up warmers. 3.5 hours is within the 4 hour time limit of holding for safety. Take care to turn warmer back up after breakfast in order to hot hold food at the proper temperature.

3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-202.16: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance. 

The shelf above the three part sink has corners that are chipped with raw wood exposed. The counter at the left of the door to the cafeteria has a wood block area. The piece was fabricated to cover the old milk coolers. Seal raw wood areas in the kitchen to facilitate cleaning.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser. 

Observed forks in a bucket for students to self serve. These forks were presented laying down with handles and tines mixed. The forks were discarded and placed into a proper container with handles presented. Person arranging forks wore single use gloves.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(1)  (P) Refried beans are 121°F. Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 135°F, or above. Reviewed hot holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was rapidly reheated to above 165°F. Reference 3-501.16(A)(1).

Observed refried beans in hot holding to be 121°F both at start and end of inspection. PIC rapidly re-heated beans to 135°F. Discussed maintaining hot holding at 135°F or above. COS.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on fan and exterior of dish washer. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

Observed accumulation of dust on fan within kitchen. Discussed routine cleaning of fan with PIC. COS.
Observed large accumulation of lime debris on the exterior of the dish washer. Discussed routine cleaning of top of dish washer with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
Lidded employee beverage found stored on a preparation table with and above clean utensils. Box of clean gloves noted stored on preparation table near beverage. Discussed proper storage areas and beverage was relocated. 
->Employee beverage noted stored in the food preparation area. Provide designated area for drinking.  (Reference 2-401.11.)

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
4 pans of cooked diced chicken 125F-130F found hot holding in hot holding cabinet near cente bank. Staff indicated chicken was cooked to temperatures above 165F and placed into cabinet ~30 minutes prior to inspection. Chicken was reheated in oven to greater than 165F. Thermostat on cabinet was raised to maximun at the time of inspection. 
->Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 135°F, or above. Reviewed hot holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. (Reference 3-501.16(A)(1).)

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
Chicken strips in wraps 55F stored in clam shell containers located in the walk-in cooler and were found double stacked. Noted staff preparing items upon arrival of inspection. Clam shell containers were opened and placed onto shallow sheet pan for more rapid cooling.
->The method of cooling in covered containers is inadequate. Food must be uncovered during cooling, if protected from overhead contamination. Discussed HACCP concept with the person in charge. (Reference 3-501.15.)

findings.title: Wholesome, sound condition
findings.comment: Three cans of tuna are observed to be dented in the dry storage area. 750-100 Food shall be in sound condition, free from spoilage, filth, and other contamination and shall be safe for human consumption. These cans were removed from the shelf and placed on the desk to be returned. violation corrected.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: Raw wood pieces are used to cover holes in the serving line at both ends. 750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.  Seal or remove wood and replace with sealed easily cleansable surface.
